title: Name who is in each scene
statement: When generating story pictures, name for each scene who is in the frame and who is not, since one shared cast list put characters where the text has none.
example: With one cast list for every scene, six of nine pictures had to be regenerated.
detail: A reading lesson's pictures were first generated with one three-person cast for every scene, and the model put people where the story does not, among them a stranger at the family's table before he has met them and in the celebration crowd after he has betrayed them. Six of nine pictures were regenerated. The fix was a second, two-person cast that names who is in frame and who is not, with explicit ALONE and NOT present wording in the scene line, and the notes say to treat a scene's cast as content, not styling. A character shown before the text brings him in is what media-never-runs-ahead-of-the-text forbids.
against: Notes for a video generator advise against negatives: "Never write "no X" in a positive prompt; it reinforces X. State the desired thing positively instead ("mouth closed, calm smile", not "not talking")." (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/extras/video-recut-drafts-2026-08-31.md`, lines 10-11). The two notes concern different generators, and neither reports a comparison of the two wordings.

evidence.quote: The first pass used one three-person cast for every scene, and the model put people where the story does not: the mother at the market, in the valley and at the split ground; the stranger at the family's table before he has met them, and grinning in the celebration crowd after he has betrayed them. Six of nine were regenerated. The fix was a second, two-person cast that names who is in frame **and who is not**, plus explicit "ALONE" / "NOT present" wording in the scene line.
treat a scene's cast as content, not styling.
